body_markdown:
KAI Proximity is a new proximity targeting capability in KNOREX XPO that lets advertisers build aggregated, location-driven audiences through real-world points of interest (POIs) sorted by category, keyword and location, to be used in Programmatic, Meta Ads and Google Ads campaigns.


Where people go can provide many clues about what they are looking for. For instance, a shopper near a car dealership may be in the market for a new vehicle, or have some level of interest in one. A visitor near a gym may care about fitness gear, or be looking to sign up for a new membership. Proximity targeting turns such real-world signals into intelligence for relevant ad targeting.


Since we[introduced proximity targeting in XPO](https://www.knorex.com/blog/2023/04/24/proximity-targeting/) , our customers have used it to reach prospects located within the vicinity of their target locations with strong results. KAI Proximity is the next iteration of proximity targeting in XPO. It gives you more control and flexibility to target the exact places you want, see them on a map and turn them into campaign-ready geo lists.


## Does proximity targeting work?


Location is one of the strongest signals of purchase intent a marketer can use, and the research backs it up:

The challenge is no longer whether location works. It is how effectively you can turn the right locations into an audience that converts.


## How KAI Proximity can help


Building a location-driven audience used to mean a lot of manual work: hunting down addresses, cleaning spreadsheets and uploading CSV files. That approach works if you know which stores you want to target, but it’s unworkable if you are targeting “every car dealership in New York” or “coffee shops within 3 miles of our new stores.”


KAI Proximity removes that manual step. Instead of starting with a file, you start with a question: what are the relevant places, and where? The platform searches for matching POIs and shows you the results before you deploy them to an ad campaign.


Of course, we’ve kept the “classic” options for familiarity. A single geo list can be created three ways:


- **Upload CSV File:** bring your own list of locations.
- **Upload KML File:** upload polygon coordinates for precise custom areas (Programmatic campaigns only).
- **Proximity Search:** find key places that match your selected categories and locations.


## How does KAI Proximity work?


KAI Proximity turns a search for places into a geo list in five steps.


### Step 1: Choose your platforms


Select the platforms the geo list will run on: Programmatic, Meta Ads, Google Ads, or any combination of them. One list can be reused easily across all three.


### Step 2: Pick a country


Searches cover one country at a time, so results stay relevant to your market.


### Step 3: Set your category and location filters


Categories follow a three-level hierarchy: Domain, Category and Sub-category. Select a whole domain such as “Automotive” to include every category under it, or pick specific ones such as “Car Dealers and Leasing.” In the Location field, type a city, ZIP code, street address, latitude/longitude or a place name or keyword, such as “Tesla.” Combine category and location with AND to narrow your results, or OR to widen them.


### Step 4: Tweak the radius


When your locations include latitude/longitude coordinates, use Advanced Settings to set the search radius around them. The default is about 3 miles. A larger radius may return more places, but it can also take longer to process and potentially become less specific.


### Step 5: Review, refine and save


KAI Proximity plots every matching POI on a map and shows the total number of locations and your estimated reach. Remove any locations that you don’t want, and both numbers update automatically. Change a filter and click Update Filter to refresh the results. When it looks right, click Save.


Running a large search? A geo list can hold up to 10,000 locations. If your results exceed that, KAI Proximity can split them into multiple geo lists for you once you confirm, so you can add them all to your campaign. If your filters match more than 50,000 locations, KAI Proximity asks you to narrow them, for example by adding a city or choosing sub-categories.


Existing geo lists can be edited in the same way. Add to or remove from your current list, and see the impact on the map before you save.

## Who should use proximity targeting?


Any brand whose customers are shaped by where they go can use KAI Proximity. A few examples:


Industry Places to target Why it works


Automotive Car dealers, auto parts stores, repair and maintenance Reach people around the places where vehicles are bought and serviced


Retail Competitor stores, malls, complementary businesses Reach shoppers around the stores that matter to your brand


Food and beverage Restaurants, cafes and dining areas near your locations Reach people around dining spots near your locations


Health and fitness Gyms, clinics, sports venues Reach people around fitness and health venues


Travel and hospitality Airports, hotels, attractions Reach people around travel hubs and destinations


Financial services Car dealers, real estate offices, universities Reach people around places linked to major purchases


## Benefits of KAI Proximity


### 1. Build audiences from real places, not spreadsheets


Search for the places your customers visit instead of compiling address files by hand. A brief like “car dealerships in New York” becomes a search, and the results become a geo list.


### 2. See your audience before you spend


Every matching location appears on a map, with the total number of locations and estimated reach beside it. You know exactly what you are targeting before the campaign goes live.


### 3. Precise control over who is included


Three levels of categories, AND/OR filter rules and an adjustable radius let you go as broad or as narrow as the campaign needs. Remove any single location, and the totals update right away.


### 4. One geo list across channels


Use the same list on Programmatic, Meta Ads and Google Ads campaigns. Targeting stays consistent wherever your ads run.


### 5. Save large searches as multiple lists


When a search returns more than 10,000 locations, KAI Proximity can split the results into multiple geo lists, so you can still target every matching location.


## How do you get the best results from KAI Proximity?


- **Start specific, then widen.** Use sub-categories and a city or ZIP code to create a tight, relevant list. Switch to OR or a broader category only if the reach is too limited.
- **Use the map as a quality check.** Scan for clusters in the wrong area or places that don’t fit your brief, and remove them before saving.
- **Match the radius to the area.** When searching around coordinates, use a smaller radius in dense cities and a larger one for wider, less dense areas.
- **Watch estimated reach as you edit.** It updates with every change, so you can balance precision against scale before the campaign goes live.
- **Name lists clearly.** Include the market, category and date (for example, “US – Car Dealers – Nov 2026”) so teams can reuse them.
- **Reuse one list across channels.** Select Programmatic, Meta Ads and Google Ads together to keep targeting consistent everywhere.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is proximity targeting?


−


Proximity targeting is a form of location-based advertising that shows ads to people near specific places, such as stores, venues or landmarks. It helps brands reach audiences based on where they are and the places they visit.


### What is KAI Proximity?


−


KAI Proximity is a feature in KNOREX XPO that finds points of interest by category, keyword and location, then saves them as geo lists for Programmatic, Meta Ads and Google Ads campaigns.


### What is a POI in advertising?


−


A POI, or point of interest, is a specific real-world place, such as a store, restaurant, gym or airport. Advertisers use POIs to reach people around the places that matter to their campaign.


### How is proximity targeting different from geofencing?


−


Geofencing draws a virtual boundary around one area. KAI Proximity starts from the type of place, finds every matching location in your chosen country and locations, and saves them as a geo list. If you need custom boundaries, you can upload a KML file for Programmatic campaigns.


### Which ad platforms does KAI Proximity support?


−


Geo lists built with KAI Proximity can be used on Programmatic, Meta Ads and Google Ads campaigns. KML polygon uploads are supported for Programmatic campaigns only.


### What is the default search radius?


−


The default radius is about 3 miles. It applies when you search around latitude/longitude coordinates, and you can change it under Advanced Settings.


### What happens if my search returns more than 10,000 locations?


−


A geo list can hold up to 10,000 locations. KAI Proximity shows how the results will be split into several geo lists named after your original list, and you confirm before saving. Add all of the lists to your campaign to target every location.


## Final words


KAI Proximity turns “where are my customers?” into a campaign-ready audience. Search by category and location, check the results on a map, trim what you don’t need, and launch across Programmatic, Meta Ads and Google Ads from your geo lists.


KAI Proximity (Beta) is available now in XPO. Existing users can find it under **Utility → Geo Lists → + Geo List → New Geo List (KAI Proximity)** .
